value.body: A two-year master's degree in social work that combines theory with supervised fieldwork in communities, hospitals, NGOs, schools and companies. Most programmes offer specialisations such as community development, medical and psychiatric social work, family and child welfare, and human resource management / labour welfare.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Usually 4 semesters with concurrent fieldwork and a block placement

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (some universities prefer a BSW or social sciences). Admission is through CUET-PG at central and many state universities — TISS has used CUET-PG scores for its master's admissions — or through a university's own entrance test and interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: Fieldwork is a large part of the course, so the institute's agency links matter for what you learn.
Common work: NGOs and development projects, CSR teams, hospitals, counselling and child protection services, and HR roles.
Starting pay in the voluntary sector is often modest; government social-welfare and project posts are another route.

value.title: Students enrolled in MSW
value.note: Programme row 'M.S.W. - Master of Social Work'. In 2023-24 about half were in distance mode (~52,600 of ~1.02 lakh), and much of the rise came from distance enrolment. AISHE counts responding institutions only; coverage varies by year, so part of any change can reflect reporting rather than real growth.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 11, programme-wise enrolment, all modes, actual responses (Ministry of Education)
